summary: Round 17 re-check, 27 Sep ~11:00-11:15Z. At the 11:01:09Z poll header probes 43/44 were PENDING and 42 exp70b was COMPLETE at 0.954. R8 closes at 12:00Z, so nothing re-checked here can be submitted, and the R15-A1 FREEZE also bars knob rungs. The 45 items re-checked in rounds 2-16 and the closed list were skipped. Three ideas had never been re-checked; all three verdicts are upheld, and in each case the old reason is replaced by a sharper one. (A) The node-addition family: DoG missing-track rescue plus the Ultrack optional-node ILP, rejected in v3 (i) for runtime and value. The 12 h limit does NOT remove the runtime objection: on K2 the in-kernel 8.0 h insertion gate binds (slack >= 0.46 h against a DoG cost of 0.9-1.4 h serial). The value objection is stronger than v3 knew: on x138, 71% of missed GT nodes already have an unclaimed predicted node 7-10 um away (and only 4.6% are merges), so a rescue mostly adds duplicates. Node levers also change sign by embryo (annotation density 0.79% vs 5.20%), which is a private risk. Upheld; for after the deadline, the lever is re-placing (z-localising) those nodes, not adding new ones. (B) The dorado out-of-sample lab (v2, dropped). D1 (dc0.30: lab +0.0013, public -0.005) makes division-knob transfer the one open question, and dorado cannot answer it: its pseudo-GT has no forks, so the division term goes unjudged, and dorado IS the 44b6 recording, which DeepCenter was trained on. Upheld. After the deadline, the only honest division-transfer bed is leave-one-embryo-out with OOF DeepCenter and DaughterNet, which means retraining. (C) Two-tail consensus (v3 (i)). One premise is stale: 'the hedge comes free from F2 = exp52/exp51' no longer holds, because F2 is now #38, a near-copy of #37. Round 15 already showed that #38's insertion hedge beats a diverse F2 on P(above the x138 block). The core objection stands: the vote collapses to 'x138 with the flow prior off', a relink class that went 0/3 on the LB. The time objection also stands, through the 8.0 h and 9.5 h internal gates. Upheld. No pre-deadline action, no build, no submit. There are curator lines only, plus one framing correction: the '~4 h headroom' is not usable on the K2 stack.

findings.what: DoG missing-track rescue and the Ultrack-style optional-node ILP / keep-clearance peaks (v3 FINAL_REPORT section i: 'ILP already selects nodes for free; DoG 0.9-1.4 h CPU under the timer'; v2 r1_dedupe dropped ultrack-optional-node-ilp / ilp-keep-clearance-peaks). LoG shoulders belong to the same family. OLD VERDICT: refuted. DoG: reachable pool 90-150 FN, net lab -0.001..+0.0005, P(gate fail) ~0.9, and 0.9-1.4 h serial on the hidden run. Optional nodes: the ILP (appearance 0, disappearance 2) already selects nodes by temporal consistency at zero node cost; probe 4 (det 0.95) = neutral; +1% nodes = -0.0009. WHAT CHANGED: (1) the 12 h limit with K2 at L (7.36, 7.54] h looks like ~4.5 h of room. (2) The base is x138 with readmit, gapfill and lowrefine. (3) Public is one embryo and private is the other ~71%. RE-DERIVED: (a) RUNTIME: NOT relieved. On any K2-family file the binding limit is the per-clip 8.0 h DIVINS gate (tools/build_probe_kernel.py l.1407-1416), not 12 h. The slack is >= 0.46 h, below the 0.58 h run spread (round 7 R7-RC-C). Even the K2'' pair (37800/32400 s) leaves 1.46 - 0.58 = 0.88 h, below DoG's 0.9 h lower bound. Late clips would lose the insertion, which is the +0.001 mechanism. (b) VALUE: stronger than v3's reason. Round 7's x138 anatomy found 668 missed GT nodes: 83% have no presafe node within 4 um, but 71% have an UNCLAIMED final node at 7-10 um (|dz| ~4.7 um), and only 4.6% are merges. The residual FN mass is therefore misplaced nodes of seen nuclei, not absent peaks. A DoG or optional node there becomes a second node for the same blob (the clearance gate rejects it, or it adds a duplicate), and LoG shoulders address the 4.6% merge share. (c) PRIVATE: node-count levers flip sign by embryo. Lab annotation density per predicted node is 0.79% on 44b6 vs 5.20% on 6bba, and readmitted-node drop measured 44b6 -0.0023 vs 6bba +0.0008 (round 12 R12-NF), so any added-node lever carries an embryo-dependent sign on the 71% private share. NEW VERDICT: UPHELD, on runtime, value and private risk. After the deadline, the lever behind this FN mass is re-localising the 7-10 um unclaimed nodes (z-placement of already-detected nuclei), not adding nodes.

findings.what: The dorado out-of-sample lab (v2 r2_research_dorado-oos-lab; v2 FINAL_REPORT Dropped: 'nothing is left for it to gate; stage 1 would finish too late; it is the same embryo as 44b6'). OLD VERDICT: dropped. The premise (in-sample lab optimism: ef +0.016 lab -> LB 0) was accepted, but no item remained to gate. WHAT CHANGED: D1 (CONTEXT 27 Sep 04:58Z) shows the exp60 lab sign is WRONG for a division knob on the unseen public embryo: DeepCenter safe-div 0.25 -> 0.30 measured +0.0013 on the honest 6bba bed and ~0 on 44b6, but -0.005 on public. D2 showed fm45 positive on public. So the question behind the class-C letter, the exp70b letter and every post-deadline division idea is now 'does a division knob transfer to an unseen embryo'. An out-of-sample bed is exactly what that needs, which is a revival case on its face. RE-DERIVED: dorado cannot answer it, for two structural reasons. (1) Its Ultrack pseudo-GT has NO forks. The research file's own protocol says 'report adjusted edge J only and treat the division term as unjudged' (and the arithmetic verifier: 'the pseudo-GT has no forks, so it is unjudgeable'). (2) dorado IS the 44b6 recording: 63/71 44b6 train clips are space-time crops of it (CONTEXT 23 Sep 23:30Z L3 finding), and the 44b6 clips are DeepCenter's training clips (CONTEXT round 13 record (5), FACTS F-DAT-12). So it is in-sample for exactly the DC stage whose transfer failed. Its free late-frame boxes (t >= 300) add nothing for private transfer (transfer verifier). NEW VERDICT: UPHELD, and the reason is sharper: it cannot judge divisions, and for DC it is in-sample. It also cannot inform the pending letters about exp70b (fm45) or 43/44 (DC 0.20/0.225) before 29 Sep. After the deadline, an honest division-transfer bed needs leave-one-embryo-out OOF DeepCenter and DaughterNet (retraining, R9) plus scoring on 6bba only. No existing bed does this.

findings.what: Two-tail consensus (v3 FINAL_REPORT section i: 'reduces to x138 without the flow prior, doubles repair time'; v_ensembles-and-private_two-tail-consensus_value/_schedule: 'the hedge already comes free from F2 = exp52/exp51'). OLD VERDICT: refuted, for three reasons. (1) Value: the majority vote collapses to 'x138 with the flow prior off', a relink-knob change, and <= ~1.5% of GT edges are linking-type errors. (2) Schedule: it doubles repair seconds against the 27000 s guard, and the x138 tail is not image-free. (3) Hedge: F2 already supplies the diversity. WHAT CHANGED: (a) the 12 h limit; (b) F2 is no longer exp52/exp51 but #38, the twin: K2 without the insertion, a near-copy of #37 that differs by ~13 dummy insertion forks, so the 'free hedge' premise is stale; (c) the public/private split and the tie rule make finals diversity matter in principle. RE-DERIVED: (a) the time objection stands. The K2 stack's own gates bind (8.0 h insertion, 9.5 h safetail repair deadline 34200 s; slack >= 0.46 h, round 7 R7-RC-C), and a second full tail is hours, not minutes. (b) The stale premise does not revive the idea: round 15 (R15-RC-C) computed that a diverse F2 loses to #38's insertion hedge on the utility that matters, P(above the ~350-team x138 block) ~0.94 vs ~0.89. Both finals have already run on the hidden set, so a consensus file could only enter as a new final, and that is barred by R8 at 12:00Z. (c) The core value argument is unchanged and is backed by LB evidence: the link-stage family is 0/3 (relink off -0.002, learned bonus -0.002, gshift -0.002; round 9 R9-RC-B), and the flow prior is what lets the head work on x138. NEW VERDICT: UPHELD. The correction is only to the record: the hedge premise now reads 'F2 = #38 supplies an insertion hedge, not diversity'.

findings.what: The research-round task text still lists '12 h limit with ~4 h headroom' as a fact that could revive old ideas. Since round 7 (R7-RC-C), that headroom is known to be unusable on the K2 stack: the per-clip 8.0 h DaughterNet gate binds, with slack >= 0.46 h, below the 0.58 h run spread. The K2'' pair (37800/32400 s) gives ~0.9 h after the spread. The finals #37/#38 have already run on the whole hidden set, so headroom is worth 0 for them. Re-checks A and C both hit this. A future agent reading '~4 h' may re-propose runtime-hungry stages.
